paragraphs: Friend, three rounds of questions came at Jesus in this passage, and the first two were traps. The Pharisees and Herodians wrapped theirs in compliments, and the Sadducees brought a seven-brothers puzzle to make the resurrection look silly. Jesus saw through both and answered with the truth. When He says, "Give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's," He is reminding them that the coin carries Caesar's image, and that they belong to God (Mark 12:17).

Then He tells the Sadducees, "Aren't you mistaken, because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God?" (Mark 12:24). Friend, that one lands on me too, because I've heard a verse and decided I already knew what it meant. Jesus teaches that the dead will rise, and He points to the burning bush, where God said, "I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob" and then says He "is not the God of the dead, but of the living" (Mark 12:26-27). That means death is not the end of the story, so the resurrection is a real hope you can stand on, and it's why we keep coming back to the Word and trusting the God whose power the Sadducees missed.

The scribe asks the one question that isn't a trap, and Jesus gives him the heart of it all: love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, mind and strength, and "Love your neighbor as yourself" (Mark 12:30-31). The scribe says that loving this way is "more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices" (Mark 12:33). And Jesus tells him, "You are not far from the kingdom of God" (Mark 12:34). So, baker, here is the big idea: know the Word, and let it lead you to love God with everything you've got and to love the people right next to you.
